Order 
This is second application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 (Section 439 of the Cr.P.C., 1973) for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.210/2024, dated 12.8.2024 registered at Police Station Narmada Nagar, District Khandwa (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 506, 509(B), 506-B, 376(2)(N) and 450 of IPC.

entities.text: Police Station Narmada Nagar, District Khandwa
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Applicant is in detention since 13.8.2024.
2 .

Applicant's first bail application was dismissed as withdrawn and not pressed vide order dated 23.10.2024 passed by this Court in M.Cr.C. No.42456 of 2024.
3 .
As per the prosecution story, on 12.8.2024, 33 years old prosecutrix submitted an application in writing before the Police stating that Ritik of the village is troubling her for the last two years.
She had lodged an FIR against him about attempt to outrage her modesty.
Ritik is threatening her to enter NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:11912 2 MCRC-9209-2025 into compromise in the case of attempt to outrage her modesty.
It is alleged that on 12.1.2023 at around 11 P.M., she was alone in her home.
Someone knocked her door.
She opened the door and it was Ritik.
After threatening to eliminate her and her children, Ritik committed rape upon her.
Being scared of the incident, she did not narrate the incident to anyone.
Thereafter, on 23.10.2023, Ritik again committed rape upon her.
On 3.5.2024, her husband had gone to Indore.

Now he is troubling much, therefore, she narrated the incident to her husband and sister.
FIR was registered.
4 . Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
Prosecutrix is 33 years old whereas, he is only 21 years old.
FIR has been lodged after considerable delay.
It is further contented that the prosecutrix has already been examined before the trial Court.
Therefore, it is prayed that applicant may be released on bail, pending the trial.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State as well as counsel for the objector have opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the applicant.
6. Prosecutrix has already been examined before the trial Court.
Now, there is no possibility of influencing of prosecution witnesses and tampering with the prosecution evidence.

Therefore,
having taken into consideration the submissions put forth by learned counsel for the applicant and material on record, but without expressing anything on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre-trial detention of the applicant is not NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:11912 3 MCRC-9209-2025 warranted.

Consequently, this bail application under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 (Section 439 of CrPC, 1973) for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant,
stands allowed.
7 . It is directed that applicant - Ritik Sen be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of BNSS, 2023 [Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C., 1973].
8 . This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
